episode_title: Building a Better Optometry Practice: 3 Doctors, 3 Big Ideas
question: Should an optometrist buy or lease a building when opening a new practice?
transcript_excerpt: Gurpreet Lika advises optometrists to pursue owning their own building rather than leasing, as it provides long-term asset growth and allows them to retain the real estate even if they sell the practice later. He took 15 years to achieve this goal, but believes the advantages of ownership—including being able to retire and still collect rent from the strata—make it worth the investment and effort.

episode_title: Building a Better Optometry Practice: 3 Doctors, 3 Big Ideas
question: What location factors should optometrists evaluate when opening a new practice?
transcript_excerpt: Key location factors include proximity to existing practices (Gurpreet's new location is an eight-minute drive from Royal Look Optometry), neighborhood affluence and patient demographics (he chose the second highest-end neighborhood in Victoria), and whether it's a place you'd be willing to drive to in 10-15 years regardless of where you live. The location should also accommodate overflow from existing practices and serve as a backup plan in case primary office developments occur.

episode_title: Building a Better Optometry Practice: 3 Doctors, 3 Big Ideas
question: How does office aesthetics and design affect patient spending in an optometry practice?
transcript_excerpt: Office design significantly influences patient spending behavior. Gurpreet observed that when the same patients and doctors are in a newly renovated, modern space versus an older facility, patients in the new location spend considerably more on eyewear. After six months, the new oceanfront practice already shows higher average sales per patient, suggesting that aesthetic elevation increases patient willingness to spend on premium products.

episode_title: Building a Better Optometry Practice: 3 Doctors, 3 Big Ideas
question: What support services does OSI offer to optometry practice owners?
transcript_excerpt: OSI provides multiple business support services beyond being a buying group, including staff coaching, process improvement, lease negotiation assistance, inventory management, and key performance indicator tracking. Gurpreet noted that he initially viewed OSI only as a discount buying group but later discovered they offer extensive business consulting through team members like Tricia who help with efficiency improvements and staff training.

episode_title: Building a Better Optometry Practice: 3 Doctors, 3 Big Ideas
question: Why is mentorship critical for success in optometry practice ownership?
transcript_excerpt: Gurpreet credits mentorship as the most important factor in his success, more than any business process or strategy. He emphasizes seeking guidance from experienced optometrists like Dr. Paul Newman and Dr. Nick White, learning from their experiences at conferences, and sharing those lessons with his team and partners. Without this mentorship network, he believes he would not have achieved his current level of success.
